title: Which vectors share a sign?
hook: One dividing line turns vectors into candidate bits.

knows: Cartesian coordinates and Euclidean distance where geometry is used; integer counts/sets as explicitly drawn.
Dot product and nonzero-vector angular similarity.
doesNotKnow: Compute hyperplane sign hashes while distinguishing a finite collision from conditional angular collision probability.

objective: Compute hyperplane sign hashes while distinguishing a finite collision from conditional angular collision probability.
misconception: Sharing a hash bit guarantees the nearest or most similar vector.

claims.text: Nonzero vectors a=(1,0),b=(1,1),c=(−1,1). Primary normal(1,0); contrast normal(0,1). Bit1 iff n·v≥0, including exact dot0.

Gaussian random normal, dot-zero convention and Pr(collision)=1−θ/π. Fixed normals here are chosen illustrations, not random samples.

claims.text: Primary dot products1,1,−1 give bits1,1,0; a and b collide. Rotated normal dots0,1,1 give bits1,1,1 under the explicit zero-dot convention.

claims.text: A one-bit collision retains candidates but does not guarantee nearest or most similar. Fixed normals can collide vectors with different angles.
